parsed.mechanism: The function mutates scheduler.__class__ to a dynamically-created subclass that captures a closure over `built` (the optimizer object). This closure is stored in the class attribute `_unsloth_legacy_resume`, and the comment says it is set on the class not the instance to avoid pickling issues. However, the closure references `built`, which is a live optimizer instance that may not be picklable (e.g., contains GPU tensors or non-picklable attributes). When a checkpoint is saved, the scheduler's state_dict includes the class attribute `_unsloth_legacy_resume` which holds this closure, and torch.save will attempt to pickle it, causing a pickle error on the first save, even when no resume is performed.
parsed.trigger: Any call to `create_scheduler` with an optimizer built by `_create_unsloth_optimizer` (i.e., when `embedding_learning_rate` is set), followed by a `trainer.save_model()` or checkpoint save that serializes the scheduler state.
parsed.consequence: The first checkpoint save fails with a pickle.PicklingError/TypeError, breaking training and resume, contradicting the stated goal of preserving scheduler state across checkpoints. The fix defeats its purpose and introduces a regression.
